input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Spirit Airlines

output.company: Spirit Airlines, LLC (formerly Spirit Airlines, Inc.); assessment as of 2026-11-09

ownership.value: Wholly owned airline subsidiary of Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. Since the March 12, 2025 emergence transaction, the former Spirit Airlines, Inc. has been Spirit Airlines, LLC; former equity was cancelled and new holding-company equity was distributed under the creditor restructuring. Both airline and holding company subsequently entered Chapter 11. No later completed ownership transfer verified.

financials.metric: Latest verified standalone operating income or EBITDA
Month-end cash reported for Spirit Airlines debtor; not verified as unrestricted available liquidity
financials.stated_by: ElevenFlo transcription of Spirit Airlines, LLC September 2026 monthly operating report, docket 1748

financials.metric: Total standalone debt, including debt subject to compromise
Current available revolver or other committed liquidity

debt_events.summary: Spirit Airlines, LLC filed Chapter 11, case 25-11896, jointly administered with the holding-company case 25-11897. This is an actual insolvency proceeding, not merely a prospective default risk.

Spirit announced immediate orderly wind-down and cancellation of all flights. The company said it could not procure the hundreds of millions of dollars of additional liquidity needed to sustain operations.
The bankruptcy case update reports an ongoing wind-down under the May 8 order, with asset-sale procedures still being pursued; the case has not returned to normal airline operations.

credit_ratings.summary: S&P withdrew all Spirit Airlines LLC ratings, including EETCs, because sufficient information to maintain the ratings was unavailable. No current S&P rating or outlook established as of the assessment date.
Fitch withdrew its Long-Term Issuer Default Rating (WD). This is a withdrawal, not an improvement in creditworthiness; no active Fitch issuer rating or outlook established.

missing_fields: Standalone annual financials: latest opened 2025 Form 10-K is Spirit Aviation Holdings consolidated accounts; not substituted for airline-only figures. April MOR also consolidates certain balances.
output.risk_rationale: As of November 9, 2026, Spirit is an insolvency-and-recovery exposure rather than a normally operating airline: it entered Chapter 11 on August 29, 2025 and cancelled all flights in the May 2, 2026 wind-down after failing to secure needed liquidity. September debtor cash of $202.8 million is not verified unrestricted liquidity or evidence that unsecured claims will be paid in full; vendor guidance routes outstanding claims through bankruptcy, while S&P and Fitch withdrew their ratings in May 2026. Avoid unsecured credit or reliance on ordinary-course performance; any wind-down transaction requires confirmation of the contracting debtor, payment priority and cash protection.

distress_signals.summary: All flights cancelled immediately as the airline began winding down. Spirit stated no additional funding was available, making ordinary-course passenger-service performance unavailable.

An employee-focused bankruptcy newsletter, citing the September monthly operating report, reported only 63 full-time employees as of October 1, 2026, versus 9,229 at the report’s historical baseline. This is secondary reporting of court-filed figures, not independently audited workforce data.

The company announced it would stop SEC periodic and current filings, unless legally required, following its wind-down decision and suspension of reporting obligations. Consequently historical annual-report cash is not evidence of present available liquidity.

payment_behaviour.summary: Company vendor guidance reviewed as of the assessment date says outstanding claims must be addressed through Chapter 11. Vendors specifically retained for wind-down work are told they can expect payment for go-forward goods and services; that statement is not assurance that historical claims will be paid in full.
